learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will master advanced rules of Concord (Subject-Verb Agreement), ensuring verbs agree with complex subjects, collective nouns, and indefinite pronouns.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 When a Subject and a Verb go on a date, they have to agree! If the subject wears a singular hat, the verb must wear one too. But what happens when the subject wears a disguise? Let's crack the code of Concord! 🕵️‍♂️

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Two subjects joined by 'and' make a plural subject (take a plural verb). BUT, if subjects are joined by 'or' or 'nor' (like Either...or / Neither...nor), the verb agrees with the subject CLOSEST to it!
examples_or_templates: Joined by And: The cat AND the dog ARE playing. (Plural)
Joined by Or/Nor: Neither the coach nor the PLAYERS WERE ready. (Agrees with 'players')
Either the players or the COACH WAS ready. (Agrees with 'coach')

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Words that don't refer to a specific person are called Indefinite Pronouns. Words like Everyone, Everybody, Someone, Nobody, Each, and Every are ALWAYS treated as SINGULAR, even though they feel like a crowd!
examples_or_templates: EVERYONE IS invited to the party. (Not 'are')
EACH of the boys HAS a bicycle. (Not 'have'. Focus on 'Each', not 'boys'!)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Measurements of time, distance, or money are treated as a single unit (Singular verb). Also, phrases like 'along with' or 'as well as' do NOT make a subject plural. Only look at the first subject!
examples_or_templates: Distance: Fifty miles IS a long way to walk. (Not 'are')
Along with: The captain, along with his crew, WAS saved. (Agrees with 'captain', ignore the crew!)

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Choose the correct verb: 'Neither my brothers nor my sister ______ going to the park.'
❓ Choose the correct verb: 'Ten thousand dollars ______ a lot of money.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with is/are: 'Everyone in the classroom _______ looking at the board.'
subjective_practice.hint: Remember the rule for indefinite pronouns like 'everyone'.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Correct the error in this sentence: 'The teacher, as well as the students, are going on the trip.'
subjective_practice.hint: When using 'as well as', the verb only cares about the very first subject (The teacher).

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Choose has/have: 'Each of the girls _______ brought her own lunch.'
subjective_practice.hint: Don't be tricked by 'girls'. The true subject is the word 'Each'.

activity_or_assignment.title: 👮‍♂️ The Grammar Police
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write down 3 tricky sentences with subject-verb agreement mistakes (like 'Nobody know the answer' or 'Five years are a long time'). Act as the Grammar Police and write out the 'tickets' explaining why they are wrong and fixing them!

chapter_summary: ⭐ With 'Either...or / Neither...nor', the verb agrees with the noun closest to it.
⭐ Indefinite pronouns like everyone, nobody, and each always take a singular verb.
⭐ Amounts, distances, and subjects followed by 'as well as' take a singular verb.
